clue.text: Young dude in Hollywood with film container

parts.note: buck is American slang for a young man, a dude
ET is Spielberg's film E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial

explanation.surface: A young Hollywood actor turns up carrying a canister of film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in Hollywood' flags that the young-man sense of buck is American.
explanation.definitionFit: A bucket is a pail, an open vessel for holding or carrying things.

clue.text: Pint-sized idol finally performing in old city

parts.note: pint-sized means very small, baby

indicators.note: only the final letter of idol

parts.note: on means performing, on stage

explanation.surface: A tiny pop idol is on stage in an ancient city.
explanation.definitionFit: Babylon was the ancient Mesopotamian capital on the Euphrates.

clue.text: Cold gypsy with goat heading to see old Stones in the round

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on taps
Rom is a Romani man, a gypsy
a goat is a lecher, a lech

indicators.note: the head, the first letter, of see

explanation.surface: A cold traveller with a goat goes to see the Rolling Stones play in the round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stones' looks like the band; it is prehistoric stone tombs.
explanation.definitionFit: Cromlechs are prehistoric megalithic monuments, often stone circles.

clue.text: Nurse with dead leg (one supporting double bass)

parts.note: EN is an enrolled nurse
pin is slang for a leg

explanation.surface: A nurse tends someone with a numb leg who props up a double bass.
explanation.definitionFit: An endpin is the metal spike at the base of a cello or double bass resting it on the floor.

clue.text: SEAL at front that's shot all over heals completely

indicators.note: the shot is all over, covering, the letter, so the letter sits inside

parts.note: a close-up is a camera shot taken near the subject

indicators.note: at front means the front letter of the word SEAL is all that is used

explanation.surface: A seal has been shot all over but its wounds mend completely.
explanation.walkthrough: SEAL looks like the animal or a verb; only its front letter is used, and 'all over' puts that S inside CLOSE-UP, a camera shot.
explanation.definitionFit: A wound closes up when it knits together and is fully mended.

clue.text: High-kicking old star slippery type knocked up

indicators.note: in a down entry, knocked up turns the word upwards, read backwards

parts.note: an eel is proverbially slippery

explanation.surface: A former kick-boxing star knocked up a slippery character.
explanation.definitionFit: Bruce Lee was a martial arts film star famous for his kicks.

clue.text: Upset person puts on ace 'Walk This Way' when drunk!

indicators.note: the person goes onto, inside, the word for ace

parts.note: an ace is a star performer

indicators.note: in a down entry, upset turns the word upwards, read backwards

parts.note: egg is old slang for a person, as in 'good egg'

explanation.surface: An upset man puts on an Aerosmith hit while drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Walk This Way' is an Aerosmith song, but here it is a description of a drunk's gait. Egg is old slang for a person, as in 'good egg'.
explanation.definitionFit: To stagger is to walk unsteadily, the gait of someone drunk.

clue.text: Sources close to Boris expect 'EU done' spiel at summits

indicators.note: the close, the last letter, of Boris
in a down entry, the tops of words are their first letters

explanation.surface: Insiders near Boris Johnson anticipate a 'Brexit done' speech at summits.
explanation.definitionFit: Seeds are origins, sources from which things grow.

clue.text: Country lover and Irishman having port put on bit of Tammy

parts.note: Pat is a typical Irish name, standing for an Irishman
Rio de Janeiro is a port

indicators.note: a single letter from the start of Tammy

explanation.surface: An Irishman drinking port sits on part of a woman named Tammy.
explanation.definitionFit: A patriot is someone who loves their country.

clue.text: We are people against old models taking the pee!

indicators.note: the old models take in the pee

parts.note: models pose, so are posers
P is the letter pee, also short for penny

explanation.surface: Objectors complain that retired models are mocking them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking the pee' looks like mockery; it puts P after O.
explanation.definitionFit: Opposers are opponents, people who are against something.

clue.text: Family express disapproval at daughter snorting line

indicators.note: taking a line up the nose, so the word for disapproval takes in the line

parts.note: to boo is to express disapproval
D is the abbreviation for daughter in genealogies

explanation.surface: Relatives jeer at a daughter caught snorting a line of cocaine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'snorting' puts L inside BOO, giving BLOO, then D follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Blood means kin or lineage, as in 'blood is thicker than water'.

clue.text: Stop to drink beer, mostly that's extremely common

indicators.note: the word for stop drinks, so takes inside it, the shortened beer

parts.note: to prevent is to stop

indicators.note: most of the word, losing its final letter

parts.note: ale is a beer

explanation.surface: Popping in for a beer before stopping is a very common habit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stop' looks like a command; it is a verb meaning prevent. 'mostly' trims ALE, and 'to drink' puts the result inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Something prevalent is widespread, found everywhere in a place or time.

clue.text: Lie about dad stealing one's sweet

indicators.note: the two words take the one in between them, as if stealing it

parts.note: to loll is to lie about lazily
pop is an informal word for a father
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A fib about father pinching someone's candy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lie about' is one phrase meaning to lounge, not a lie told about something; 'stealing' puts I between the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: A lollipop is a hard sweet on a stick.

clue.text: Good dope inhaled by excellent old racketeer!

indicators.note: breathed in by, so the first pieces go inside the word for excellent

parts.note: A1 means excellent, with the 1 read as the letter I
an ass is a dope, a fool

explanation.surface: A veteran gangster inhales some top-quality drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: A racketeer here is a tennis player with a racket: Andre Agassi, now retired.
explanation.definitionFit: Andre Agassi is a former tennis champion, so a retired player of a racket sport.

clue.text: Siren ultimately seedy, removing top to show bust

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so only the last letter of siren
the first letter of the word for seedy is removed

parts.note: seedy can mean sick, unwell

explanation.surface: A sleazy siren loses her top to display her bust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'removing top' takes S off SICK, leaving ICK; N comes from 'Siren ultimately'.
explanation.definitionFit: Nick and bust are both slang for arrest.

clue.text: Chaps on the punt will get bit of tuition for it

definitions.text: Chaps on the punt will get bit of tuition for it

parts.note: a punter, someone who bets, is a better
chaps are men

indicators.note: a single letter from the start of the word tuition

explanation.surface: Gamblers are advised that some lessons will improve their luck.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as a whole, the clue describes improvement gained through tuition.
explanation.definitionFit: Betterment is improvement, the result tuition is meant to bring.

clue.text: Knight's backing singers to secure English music producer

indicators.note: the singers hold, secure, the abbreviation inside

parts.note: the Pips sang behind Gladys Knight

explanation.surface: A knight's choir hire an English record producer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knight' looks like a title; it is Gladys Knight, whose group was the Pips.
explanation.definitionFit: The pipes, bagpipes, are an instrument that produces music.

clue.text: Junkie-looking criminal ate acid with me

indicators.note: criminal means bad or wrong, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A wasted crook dropped acid with the speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'criminal' scrambles ATE, ACID and ME.
explanation.definitionFit: Emaciated means abnormally thin and wasted, as addicts often look.

clue.text: A hugely experienced topiarist? That's Serpent!

definitions.meaning: a whimsical reading: a master of bushes, a topiarist
a large venomous snake of Central and South America

explanation.surface: Someone praises an expert hedge-clipper, then exclaims about a snake.
explanation.definitionFit: A topiarist clips shrubs, so a master of the bush; the snake is a pit viper.

clue.text: Songs and dances about a bit of debauchedness

indicators.note: the dances go around the rest

parts.note: balls are formal dances

indicators.note: a single letter from the start of debauchedness

explanation.surface: Music and dancing with a hint of decadence.
explanation.definitionFit: Ballads are narrative songs.

clue.text: Wrong move lost tempi securing vacant squares

indicators.note: the shuffled letters hold the remains of squares inside
lost means astray or confused, so the letters are rearranged
vacant means emptied, keeping only the outside letters of squares

explanation.surface: A musician loses tempo and blunders over empty squares.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost' makes MITEP from the letters of tempi; 'vacant' empties squares to SS, which 'securing' puts in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: A misstep is a stumble or blunder, a false step.

clue.text: Beware of unfinished sparkling wine close to inebriate

indicators.note: the word loses its final letter

parts.note: cava is Spanish sparkling wine

indicators.note: the close, the last letter, of the word inebriate

explanation.surface: A warning about half-drunk bubbly leaving you nearly drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfinished' cuts CAVA to CAV, and E comes from 'close to inebriate'.
explanation.definitionFit: Cave is Latin for 'beware', used as a schoolboy warning cry.

clue.text: You might say spectacles in which looker gets with listener

parts.note: an eye looks
an ear listens

explanation.surface: Someone observes that glasses are where eye and ear meet.
explanation.walkthrough: Glasses rest by both: their lenses sit before the eyes and their arms hook over the ears.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyewear is any item worn over the eyes, glasses being the typical example.

clue.text: Bit of lather over, on occasion, Knut puzzle

parts.note: suds are lather, so one sud is a bit
O is the abbreviation for over in cricket

indicators.note: only some of the time, so alternate letters of Knut

explanation.surface: King Knut is soaped up and puzzled.
explanation.definitionFit: Sudoku is a number-placing logic puzzle.

clue.text: Desire for Congress to arrest 'Titanium' musician

indicators.note: to arrest is to hold, so the word for desire holds the metal

parts.note: congress here is sexual intercourse, and desire for it is lust
Ti is the chemical symbol for titanium

explanation.surface: A political longing to arrest a songwriter named Titanium.
explanation.walkthrough: Congress looks like the US legislature; it is sex, and desire for it is lust.
explanation.definitionFit: A lutist is a lute player, a musician.

clue.text: Headdress so long that Hoskins must put on

indicators.note: the setter wears it, so goes inside the farewell

parts.note: ta-ra is an informal goodbye, like so long
the setter refers to himself, I

explanation.surface: A crown has been on so long that the setter has to wear it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'must put on' puts I inside TARA.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiara is a jewelled ornamental headband or crown.

clue.text: Reckon to have a hug of popular model of a man?

indicators.note: the word for reckon hugs, wrapping round, the word for popular

parts.note: to figure is to reckon
in means popular, fashionable

explanation.surface: Someone reckons on getting a hug from a popular male model.
explanation.walkthrough: A model man is a statuette, not a catwalk model.
explanation.definitionFit: A figurine is a small statuette, a scale model of a person.

clue.text: Easy-going couple of old men sent back food

indicators.note: returned, so the two old men are read backwards

parts.note: two words for an old man, a father: pa and da
table can mean the food served, as in 'keeps a good table'

explanation.surface: A relaxed pair of old fellows send their meal back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old men' here means fathers, pa and da; 'sent back' reverses only that pair, giving ADAP.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone adaptable adjusts readily, so is easy-going and flexible.

clue.text: No good in the sack, gutted adult admitted

indicators.note: admitted means let in through the door, so the adult is let in between the remaining letters
the inner letter is removed

parts.note: the sack is slang for bed
A is the abbreviation for adult, as in film ratings

explanation.surface: A grown-up confesses to being disappointing in bed, and feeling gutted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gutted' takes E from BED, leaving BD; 'admitted' puts A inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Bad is the opposite of good.

clue.text: Old, essentially drunk and very short as Hoskins?

indicators.note: at its essence, the central letter of drunk
the French word loses its last letter

parts.note: tres is French for very

explanation.surface: The setter admits to being old, half-cut and rather small.
explanation.walkthrough: 'essentially' takes U from drunk; 'short' cuts TRES to TRE. The setter calls himself risqué.
explanation.definitionFit: Outré means unconventional, eccentric, beyond propriety, which Hoskins's racy clues are.

clue.text: Step out with mad European in a beastly rush

indicators.note: out means wrong or disordered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Stepping out with a crazed continental leads to a frantic dash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' scrambles STEP and MAD into STAMPED, then E follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A stampede is a sudden panicked rush of a herd of animals.

clue.text: Bloody spirit gone over because of this perhaps

indicators.note: turned over, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: bloody can mean red
rum is a spirit

explanation.surface: A ghost passed over to the other side as a result of a killing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gone over' reverses REDRUM, the word made famous in The Shining.
explanation.definitionFit: A spirit goes over to the other side when someone dies, and a killing could be the cause.
